# GEO report: harbor-site **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 65–65/100, Needs work Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points). How it's calculated: low = 16.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. High = (16.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. The site is built with Astro and renders its pages on the server, which is good. The score is held back by two search crawlers blocked in `robots.txt`, broken structured data, and the same canonical address on every page. There are no unknowns. Everything was read from code, not measured on a live site. ## Live check **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Let the AI search crawlers in `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are blocked from the whole site. There is no `geo.config.json`, so I assumed you want AI search tools to find the site. If the block is deliberate, say so and I'll treat it as a choice. No cap was applied, because no policy is declared. - **Why it matters:** blocked search crawlers can't read any of your pages. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` (and the same for `PerplexityBot`) - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 77 ### 2. Repair the structured data (JSON-LD) JSON-LD is a label that tells machines what a page is. Two of your labels are broken, so they would be ignored. - **Why it matters:** the FAQ label has a blank key where `acceptedAnswer` should be. The Article label has a trailing comma, which makes it invalid JSON, and it has no author or date. - **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9` - **What the code says:** `" ": {` and `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 73 ### 3. Give each page its own canonical address A canonical link says "this is the main address of this page". - **Why it matters:** the layout points every page at the home page, so `/moorings` tells search engines it is a duplicate of `/`. - **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname`, or pass it as a prop. - **Score after this:** 71 ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is valid | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have access | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4-8`, site-wide, 0 of 3 points | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/contact.astro:4` is `noindex` but is in the sitemap and nav; 2 of 3 routes clear | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the right origin | Problem | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`; 1 of 3 routes clear (home only) | | GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Clear | Not run | Astro renders on the server, including the `client:load` form | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Problem | Not run | `src/data/faq.json:8`, `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`; 0 of 2 routes clear | | GEO-011 | Sitemap is discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml`, `Sitemap:` at `public/robots.txt:10` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Clear | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:4-7`, set on all 3 routes | | GEO-016 | Pages reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:12` uses plain `` | | GEO-017 | No snippet block against AI search | Problem | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`; 1 of 3 routes clear (`/contact`) | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read `Base.astro` and `Newsletter.jsx` (labelled input, named button, no images) | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present; not scored | ## Other problems found - `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`: ``. The default stops search tools from quoting any page that doesn't set its own value. Change the default to omit the tag or use `index, follow`. This is also the cause of GEO-017. - `public/sitemap.xml:5` lists `/contact`, which is `noindex` (`src/pages/contact.astro:4`). Remove it from the sitemap, or drop the `noindex` if you want the page found. ## Worth considering - **FAQ answers exist only in structured data:** `src/data/faq.json:18`: `"text": "Yes, from May to September."`. `src/pages/index.astro` never shows these answers as visible text. Show them on the page, and the labels then describe real content. - **Opening dates are only in the JSON:** the water taxi's May–September season appears nowhere a visitor can read it. The same applies to the price on `/moorings`: `

Prices start at £40 a night.

` is the only price, with no table of sizes. The meta description promises "Mooring sizes and seasonal prices" (`src/pages/moorings.astro:5`). - **Harbour office details could be labelled:** `src/pages/contact.astro:6`: `Call the harbour office on 01326 000000.` Marking up the phone number, address and hours (a LocalBusiness label) might help machines read them. Hours and address aren't on the page yet. - **Page basics are missing:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:5-10` has no `` or viewport tag, and pages have no `
`. - **No site URL in the Astro config:** there is no `astro.config.*` and `harbor.example` is hardcoded in several places. Setting `site` would let you build canonicals and the sitemap from one value. - **Sitemap has no ``:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-5`. Add dates if you have real ones. - **Little linking onward:** `src/pages/index.astro:7` mentions moorings and a water taxi, but only the global nav leads to `/moorings`. A link in the text might help. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Live status codes, redirects and headers:** the code can't show these, so a live scan is the way to confirm them. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools and search engines to find this site (no `geo.config.json` exists). - `https://harbor.example` is your real origin. - The three pages in the sitemap are the whole site. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
